style: Use case: stylized-concept. Production sprite for a Don't Starve Together magic wand. Reference image A is the user's actual in-game comparison: match the bold flat graphic treatment of the THREE BIG original staffs in the middle/right, angular oversized ornament, extremely strong irregular BLACK ink outline, 2-3 broad flat color regions and just 3-5 decisive woodgrain scratches. Reference image B is our approved nine wand concepts: preserve the specified material and silhouette motif. All assets in this set share the SAME line weight and muted warm-brown wood, matte ochre brass, very deep black shadows, one saturated red accent when requested. Chunky readable silhouette at 64px item resolution. Orthographic frontal 2D paper-cut illustration. Isolated real transparent alpha. No scene, no text, no labels, no glow halos, no realistic grain, no soft airbrush, no tiny etching.
specs: heads

One coherent modular HEAD atlas, exactly SIX separated compact crowns in a regular 3 columns x 2 rows. TOP ROW: single big RED diamond crystal in a thick brass/blackwood claw mount; TWO BIG RED crystal points branching from a thick mount; THREE BIG RED crystal points (middle taller) with thick claw mount. BOTTOM ROW: one broad curved RED lacquered WOOD prong; two broad curved RED WOOD tines; three broad RED WOOD tines. Bottom-row tips are matte wood showing brown woodgrain and clearly no gemstones. All six have a stout cylindrical short antique brass SOCKET at bottom, width one fifth of crown width. Overall head aspect ratio around 0.8-1.0 width to 1.0 height, much broader than the delicate references. Gems use 3-4 big facets. Thick base shoulders. Entire crown visible, 10% transparent margin in every cell. No handles or tails.
tails

One coherent modular POMMEL atlas, exactly THREE separate small pommels in one row. Left a RED teardrop gem, center a RED circular gem, right a RED diamond gem. Each framed in bold BLACK ink with a SIMPLE thick ochre brass claw frame and a WIDE flat short brass attachment rim at the TOP; rim width 55% of pommel width. Small pointed wooden tip at bottom. Full silhouette each fully visible and separated by clear transparent gutters. Pommel aspect width/height roughly 0.9. No handle, no wand head. Same simplicity and thick lines as the staffs in screenshot A.
body_01

Exactly ONE isolated wooden SHAFT MIDSECTION for concept 01 in reference B. warm hazel, an open forked wooden shoulder above and below, tapering into a smooth sculpted middle. Only the part between the head and pommel. NO gemstones, NO crown, NO dangling pommel. Both ends are centered on the same straight vertical axis, with substantial connecting shoulders and a short flat, wide joining stub each at the top and bottom. Keep the two ends around 65%-75% of the maximum shaft width, never a skinny neck. Overall long master silhouette height around 4.5 times its widest width. Upper shoulder occupies about 12% and lower heel 12% of silhouette height, middle long grip 76%; both joining stubs have matching diameter. Entire shaft fully visible, straight vertical with natural asymmetric wood bulges but aligned joint centers, 15% transparent padding.
